note: The signal is a defect that has JUST been fixed or is about to be, where nothing yet stops it recurring. Negatives are adjacent testing work that is not about locking one bug shut - gate-triage owns a red suite, automated-code-review owns rule rollout, seams-and-modularity owns testability, reference-match-loop owns proving a validator can fail.

queries.query: ok that's the third time this month someone's reintroduced the same off-by-one in the pagination helper. i've fixed it again but clearly writing it in the PR description isn't working
just patched a nasty one - our env var parser was silently returning undefined for keys with underscores so half the config was ignored. fix is in, what should i do so this can't come back
i keep wanting to add a line to CONTRIBUTING.md saying 'never call this constructor directly' but honestly nobody reads it. is there a better way to make that stick
found and fixed the bug where the retry loop swallowed the original exception. before i open the PR i want something in the suite that would have caught it
our CI has been red for two weeks with four different failures and people just merge past it now. where do i even start
queries.why: Near-miss on gate-triage: an existing suite whose red has stopped meaning anything, not locking one fixed bug shut.

queries.query: want to roll out a new eslint rule across the whole monorepo but it fires on about 900 files in packages/legacy. how do i introduce it without a giant flag-day PR
queries.why: Near-miss on automated-code-review: adopting a rule on legacy code, no specific defect being sealed.

queries.query: this OrderProcessor class is 3000 lines and reaches out to the payment gateway in its constructor so i can't get it under test at all. where do i cut it
queries.why: Near-miss on seams-and-modularity: making code testable in general, not gating one bug.

queries.query: what's the difference between a unit test and an integration test, and roughly what ratio should we be aiming for
queries.why: A general testing-philosophy question with no defect in play.

queries.query: i've got a csv of house prices with square footage, bedrooms and postcode. can you fit a regression model and tell me which variable actually explains the price
queries.why: Statistical regression. Kept as a negative because the surrounding domain is full of it and a bug-prevention skill must never surface for data modelling - this case is why the skill is not called regression-anything.

queries.query: our nightly job runs a regression suite against last week's baseline images and reports the diff. it's been passing but i don't trust it
queries.why: Near-miss: an existing regression SUITE being distrusted is reference-match-loop (prove the validator fails on known-bad), not sealing a specific fixed bug.
